newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba, prepares for polls, defends system as democratic.
newsitem.headline: Cuba, prepares for polls, defends system as democratic.

text.p: Cuba, preparing for local government elections in October, Monday defended its one-party communist system as democratic and condemned the United States for trying to get it to change.

Parliamentary president Ricardo Alarcon, speaking at a ceremony to present a new commission that will prepare the Oct. 19 election, said the United States sought to run the world and to "own the idea of democracy."
"Since 1959 (the date of President Fidel Castro's revolution) Cubans are the only owners of their land and their destiny," he said. "Our society is profoundly democratic," he added.
Calling on all Cubans to take part in the election process, Alarcon said the vote would serve to cement Cubans' patriotism and unity.
"With these elections, we will tell the world, one more time, that in Cuba it is Cubans who rule, and nobody else," he said.

Alarcon added that the United States tried to impose a model of democracy that was a "fiction" and that was laden with corruption. Political scandals in the United States were no longer news, they were as natural as the weather report, he added.
Washington is the most vocal critic of Cuba's system and maintains a 35-year embargo on the island in order to press for change. The embargo was toughened last year with new legislation.

The elections in October are for delegates to the Municipal assemblies of People's Power, the lowest tier of the legislature. The vote will be followed in the months afterwards by elections to provincial assemblies and to the National Assembly.

The October elections will be held nine days after a congress of the Communist Party. A central document issued for debate by Cubans ahead of the congress has made clear the party intends to stick with the single-party socialist system.
